US Southwest theater for Falcon BMS

An add-on theater built from real data: aerial imagery, surveyed elevation, real airfields and cities from Los Angeles to Denver.

Current release: 1.0.3

Smooth taxi and take-off roll on every airfield, no more explosions at lift-off or low over towns, sharp painted pavement at 524 airfields, airfield lights. Download, installer and updater.

Everything below is work in progress and not in the download yet. It ships together as the next update once it has been flown and checked.

What we are working on

25 November 2026

Every airfield rebuilt from real data

The largest piece of work so far. The airfields were taken apart and rebuilt layer by layer: 1,079 runways at 724 airfields checked one by one against FAA survey data, the map and our aerial photo; each airfield's own pavement with sharp paint at 708 of them; runway and taxiway lights at 615; real taxi routes and 12,081 parking spots at 780; 13,472 sign arrays; radio and approach data on the corrected runways. The sections below show the parts. Full list on the status page

Nellis AFB: the aerial photo with what the rebuild puts on it - FAA runway paint and numbers, taxi lines and hold lines, lights (coloured dots) and signs (red and yellow bars). Drawn from the model geometry, not a screenshot.

25 November 2026

Night lighting

Cities. The theater has its own night ground: 711 night tiles covering every lit place from Los Angeles to Denver. Every mapped street carries its own row of separate lamps, buildings glow dimly, and large buildings get a lit apron. How much of a place is lit follows NASA's Black Marble satellite night-lights data, so the open desert stays dark and a city street has all its lamps. Lamp colour is half warm sodium, half white LED per street; which street is which is a choice of ours, not a record.

Airfields. More than 180,000 lights at 615 airfields: white runway edge lights every 200 ft, green threshold bars, red runway end bars, blue taxiway edge lights every 150 ft, all on the real runway ends and taxiways. They follow the sim's own rule: on at night or in bad weather while an aircraft is at the field.

Not there yet. Approach light systems, PAPI and runway centreline lights (no data source lists them per runway end), lit airfield signs, and lit windows on the building models.

Central Phoenix as the night ground draws it, about 16 km across: freeways, the street grid, Sky Harbor dark in the middle. City lights are in the base download; airfield lights since 1.0.3.

25 November 2026

A roof on every building

Until now every generated building had a flat lid in the colour measured from the aerial photo. Every building now gets a roof shape: A-frame, hip or single slope, with chimneys on houses and air-conditioning units on commercial roofs. Roofs are also drawn darker, because the bright ones flickered at long range. To protect frame rate the shaped roofs are only drawn close to the aircraft; further out the simpler model is used.

beforeafter

Downtown Phoenix and housing west of Phoenix. Preview renders of the building models over the theater's aerial imagery, not in-game screenshots. Footprints, heights and wall types are real data; which roof shape a single building gets is a rule. More pictures

25 November 2026

Airfield signs at every named intersection

13,436 sign arrays at 708 airfields: red runway holding position signs, black and yellow taxiway location signs, and yellow direction signs with arrows, readable from both sides. Runway numbers, their left / right order and the taxiway names are real data. Where each sign stands and how big it is follows the FAA placement rules; the signs are not surveyed one by one.

Falcon Field, Mesa: the D7 / 4R-22L pair and a direction array, drawn from the sign geometry.

25 November 2026

Runways where they really are

At 174 airfields the runway position on file lay beside the real runway, in the worst cases by more than 2,000 ft, so lights and paint sat next to the pavement. Every runway was checked against FAA survey data, the mapped centreline and our own aerial photo. Lights, paint, taxi routes and approach data now sit on the runway you see. 37 renumbered runways also carry their current numbers.

Fort Sumner, New Mexico. Red: where lights and paint were built. Green: the corrected position, on the photographed runways.

25 November 2026

Parking: every aircraft faces its taxi lane

The sim points a parked aircraft at the taxi point listed before its spot. Our data shared one point between two spots, so thousands of aircraft stood at 45 degrees. Every one of the 12,081 spots now has its own point; 691 stands use the real stand axis from the map.

Luke AFB: taxi routes per runway direction, parking spots with their nose direction.

25 November 2026

Terrain: the towers of land

Some of you met sheer towers and pits in the south-west of the map. The cause is found: levelling shapes that belong to the stock Korea theater were being applied to our terrain, at Korean coordinates. A fix is being tested.

One of 273 places: an airbase-shaped block 4,700 ft high in the sea off Malibu.

25 November 2026

Ground imagery: square patches and colour streaks

The high-resolution ground showed squares where aerial photos of different years met, and the standard set had yellow and teal streaks from the satellite composite. The flagged pieces are being rebuilt from the source photos, one photo set per state with blended seams.
